@graph.name: Local Graph Registry Dataset — Scope
@graph.description: What this registry is and the rules it runs on. The graph’s center (Google) resolves both branches correctly; the graph’s edges (aggregators, directories, stale scrapes) corrupt them — and the edges are the layer answer engines and secondary directories actually read. This dataset is the permanent corrections worklist for that layer: branch truth generated from the estate; every public record as a field-level row with a status from a controlled vocabulary; propagation parents so a downstream row is never demanded fixed before its upstream; corrected-live earned only on direct-fetch proof; verification aging flagged, never silently trusted; collisions catalogued DO-NOT-TOUCH; and the owner’s action list generated from the rows it blocks so it cannot drift.

about.name: Local-business graph
about.description: The set of public records about the two branches across search, maps, aggregators, directories and review platforms — the corroboration layer (Claude gates: Corroborated) that answer engines read alongside the estate itself.

about.name: Branch parity
about.description: Winchester and Martinsburg are always both present in every view of this registry — coverage matrix, worklist, snapshots — and are never blended into a single company figure.

about.name: Propagation
about.description: Directory data flows downhill from aggregators. A row whose fix depends on an upstream record names that record as its propagation parent; the parent must be corrected-live and one refresh cycle must pass before the child can be judged.

scopeRules: Statuses come only from the controlled vocabulary; a status that cannot be honestly assigned is unverifiable-today, never a guess.
corrected-live requires a direct-fetch observation of the corrected public page; snippets and search results can open work, never close it.
A correct value for a branch field must trace to the generated branch entity or to a cited canonical estate record; the generator refuses a value that traces to neither.

Review data is carried as per-platform distribution snapshots — averages, counts and arithmetic — never blended across platforms or branches, and never presented as a quality signal (owner ruling 2026-10-31).
Collision companies are catalogued for detection only. This registry never edits, claims or corrects another company’s record.
No third-party record in this dataset carries a client name, a price, a contract, a clearance or a certification claim.

@graph.description: The element’s gap records, each with its evidence rows, its impact, and its designed solution — solutions, not problem lists (owner ruling 2026-10-31). gapRecords.title: Birdeye public pages contradict the completed claim
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: Re-verification pass (sketch B2) + propagation proof (sketch B7)
gapRecords.impact: A widely syndicated review platform publicly states both profiles are unclaimed, shows a wrong-direction Winchester address, and shows zero reviews for a branch Google rates 4.7/6 — every surface that syndicates Birdeye inherits all three errors.
gapRecords.solution: Re-verify both public profile URLs directly (the re-verification pass): if the post-claim state is clean, update the rows on that evidence; if not, work the in-account correction on the claimed profiles (address fix on Winchester; syndication check on Martinsburg — a claimed location showing zero Google reviews is a feed defect to raise inside the account, not a content problem) and sharpen the Martinsburg category to Movers. The registry tracks the public page, never the account claim, as the status source.

gapRecords.title: The Data Axle root record is unconfirmed; the 1850 Valley Ave cluster hangs off it
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: Data Axle root fix (sketch B3) + propagation proof (sketch B7)
gapRecords.impact: Five-plus public records carry a wrong address whose most plausible single upstream is one unconfirmed aggregator account; until the root is corrected and one refresh cycle passes, no cluster row can honestly close.
gapRecords.solution: Owner step 1 confirms the account (the confirmation link works only in the owner’s own browser); both branch corrections are then executed from the canonical packets in the same session — the highest-leverage single action in the graph. Cluster rows then re-resolve on the propagation rule: parent corrected-live + one refresh cycle, verified per row by direct fetch (sketch B7). The sequence also tests empirically whether Data Axle is the sole upstream.

gapRecords.title: BBB: a wrong-address duplicate is live and Martinsburg has no profile
gapRecords.impact: BBB is a trust surface answer engines cite; the findable profile carries the stale address and is tied to the real place by BBB’s own identifier, while the correct profile sits behind it and Martinsburg is absent.
gapRecords.solution: Owner step 3 (sign-in) inside the one consolidated sitting: merge 0241-235987783 into 0241-236010957 on the free correction path (no paid accreditation — standing rule) and create the Martinsburg profile from the canonical packet in the same session.

gapRecords.title: GreatGuysMove still displays an invented 15% discount and a license-status framing
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: Our-side stale-artifact retirements (sketch B5) + the second correction
gapRecords.impact: A mover directory attributes to the company an offer it has never made and a federal license-status framing it does not publish — both are exactly the kind of claim an answer engine lifts verbatim.
gapRecords.solution: Two-sided, sequenced: first retire our own stale pre-rebuild page carrying the identical sentence (the provenance — sketch B5), verifying it is still served before touching it; then send the second correction citing that provenance and requesting removal of both the discount and the license-status framing. The first correction (2026-10-30) is on record; the row stays open until the public page is clean on direct fetch.

gapRecords.title: The Thryv family points Winchester at a Haymarket address; Martinsburg is absent
gapRecords.impact: Three directory properties share one wrong record — wrong city, wrong address — and none carries Martinsburg; the feed will keep re-publishing the error until the single account is fixed.
gapRecords.solution: Owner step 2 (the owner sets the new Thryv account password — the one credential action no one else can do); both branch records are then corrected in the one Thryv system and Martinsburg is added as the second location. One fix covers Superpages, YellowPages and DexKnows.

gapRecords.title: Porch: self-contradicting years-in-business, missing suite, no Martinsburg profile
gapRecords.impact: A lead marketplace states the company is 4 years old on the same page that says “Since 2010” — a founding-date contradiction machines can quote either way.
gapRecords.solution: Owner step 4 (Porch sign-in) inside the consolidated sitting: correct years-in-business to since June 2010, add Suite 11, and create the Martinsburg profile from the canonical packet in the same session.

gapRecords.title: Martinsburg label drift at the center: shortened name, unpublished offering labels
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: GBP-source audit (read-only) — next sequenced batch; no owner step unless the audit shows an in-account fix
gapRecords.impact: The drift sits at the graph’s center, not its edge: an answer engine summarizing the Martinsburg branch can lift “Certified gun safe transport” as a company claim, and the shortened name weakens the branch distinction the whole estate maintains.
gapRecords.solution: GBP-source audit first (read-only manager read): if the labels and shortened name live in the GBP record, correct them at the source; if they are platform synthesis, mark the rows monitored-synthesis and hold the line that keeps synthesis honest — the estate’s published labels stay exact, so what the platform learns from is correct — and re-check on the measurement cadence. Either way the outcome lands here as a status change with evidence.

gapRecords.title: AnyFlip serves a stale mirror of the old homepage under our name
gapRecords.impact: An owned-but-stale artifact ranks for name queries carrying claims the current site does not make — self-inflicted staleness is the most fixable corruption class in the graph.
gapRecords.solution: Establish account provenance (owner step 6 only if recovery requires identifying the account email), then takedown-or-update the mirror to the current homepage. Sequenced with the /post/ retirement in sketch B5 — the same work class: our own stale artifacts are removed before asking anyone else to correct theirs.

gapRecords.title: Martinsburg’s edge coverage is thinner than Winchester’s (branch parity)
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: Owner sitting creations (sketch B4) + graph expansion wave (sketch B6, G-E5)
gapRecords.impact: Martinsburg-only sources in the audit were three (one scraped, one thin). A branch an answer engine cannot corroborate is a branch it describes thinly — the parity gap is a visibility gap, not an administrative one.
gapRecords.solution: The parity wave: every source that carries Winchester gets a Martinsburg creation task from the canonical packet — the BBB and Porch creations ride the owner sitting; the directory parity set (MapQuest, NearbyMovers, BestProsInTown, Bizidex, Bunity, HireRush, Chamber directory, Fyple and the rest of the grouped sweep) is created in the G-E5 wave. The coverage matrix in this dataset is the wave’s worklist: no source may show a blank Martinsburg cell.

gapRecords.title: Name-collision conflation is possible and currently unmonitored
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: This registry (the collision class, live in this batch) + the quarterly name-query sweep on the measurement cadence
gapRecords.impact: At least six same-name companies exist, one with federal carrier registration and one with an F-rated BBB profile; an aggregator attaching any of their identifiers, ratings or complaints to this company would currently be discovered by accident.
gapRecords.solution: The collision class in this dataset is the detection baseline: collision companies are catalogued DO-NOT-TOUCH with their distinguishing facts, so a conflation event (their identifiers on our records, or ours on theirs) is recognizable in one query. The quarterly name-query sweep on the measurement cadence checks for events; any event found becomes a record row here with the correction path for that surface.

gapRecords.title: CB Insights carries the stale HQ address and its claim path is blocked on a mailbox decision

gapRecords.impact: A company-intelligence platform read by researchers and answer engines states the wrong headquarters on a freshly crawled page, and the only unblock is an owner decision about a company-domain mailbox.

@graph.name: Local Graph Registry — Method
@graph.description: How the registry is built and maintained. (1) The canonical side is generated from the estate registries; (2) the observation side is transcribed from the evidence base — Dossier 03’s audit of 2026-10-31 and the backlink program’s records — with every row carrying its evidence reference, and the fresher source governing conflicts (conflicts are noted on the row, never silently resolved); (3) statuses follow the controlled vocabulary and the direct-fetch rule for corrected-live; (4) the coverage matrix, owner-step list and totals are computed from the rows at generation, so the published views cannot drift from the underlying records; (5) maintenance runs on the measurement cadence — re-verification passes update rows only on page evidence, stale-verification flags mark rows past the window, and every regeneration re-seals the file in the estate’s signed index in the same motion.
articleBody: Evidence tiers follow the Retrieval Machine research framework: platform documentation, the program’s own sampled reads (search-surface and Places-style records, each labeled with its method and crawl age), the backlink program’s execution records, and owner statements (labeled, never silently upgraded).

Crawl ages are stated because aggregator pages are republished on the platform’s schedule, not ours: a 210-day-old crawl showing “not been claimed” beside a claim completed yesterday is a stale observation, and the registry says so on the row instead of averaging the two into a false state.

The propagation model is tested, not assumed: the Data Axle root fix (sketch B3) followed by one refresh cycle and a per-row direct-fetch proof pass (sketch B7) will show which cluster rows actually resolve from the root — the registry’s parent links make that experiment readable row by row.

@graph.name: Local Graph Registry — Boundaries
@graph.description: What this registry will not do. It never edits, claims or corrects another company’s record (the collision class is detection-only). It never presents a review count — ours or a competitor’s — as a quality or authority signal. It never marks a row corrected on snippet evidence. It never blends the two branches. It carries no client names, no prices beyond the estate’s already-published industrial schedule (which appears nowhere in this file), no contracts, no clearances and no certification claims. Paid corrections and paid placements are outside the program’s no-paid rule; where a platform paywalls an edit (Judy’s Book), the registry records the free propagation path instead.
boundaryRules: DO-NOT-TOUCH: collision-company records are never edited by this program.
Direct-fetch rule: corrected-live is earned on the public page, not on a snippet, a dashboard claim or a submission receipt.
No-paid rule: corrections and creations use free paths; paywalled edits are recorded with their free alternative.
Branch rule: Winchester and Martinsburg are separate entities on every surface of this dataset — separate records, separate snapshots, separate cells.
Owner-step rule: the consolidated owner list is generated from the rows; an action that is not on a row is not on the list.
